text:
Predicates:
Flu(x) ::: x gets the flu.
Monkeypox(x) ::: x has Monkeypox.
Infects(y, x) ::: y causes x.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Human(x) ::: x is a human.
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Symptom(x, y) ::: x is a symptom of y.
FeelTired(x) ::: x feels tired.
Glu(x) ::: x gets a glu.
Question:  
Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? No one gets flu.

Premises:  
∀x (Monkeypox(x) → ∃y (Infects(y, x))) ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals, including humans.  
Humans(x) → Mammal(x) ::: Humans are mammals.  
Mammal(x) → Animal(x) ::: Mammals are animals.  
Symptom(Monkeypox, fever) ∧ Symptom(Monkeypox, headache) ∧ Symptom(Monkeypox, muscle pains) ∧ Symptom(Monkeypox, feeling tired) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include fever, headache, muscle pains, feeling tired, and so on.  
FeelTired(x) → ∃z (Glu(z) ∧ x = z) ::: People feel tired when they get a glu.
